clue.text: Merrymaking includes a show

indicators.note: includes says the merrymaking word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: revel means merrymaking, lively festivity

explanation.surface: A festive celebration that features some kind of performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to disclose or uncover it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Censure a metropolis for greed

parts.note: a rap is a rebuke or censure, as in a rap on the knuckles
a metropolis is a large city

explanation.surface: Someone condemns a big city for its avarice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping, plundering avarice, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Forces one may make light of

definitions.text: Forces one may make light of

parts.words: Forces one may make light of
parts.note: electromotive forces measured in volts can be used to make electric light; on the surface, forces one shrugs off

explanation.surface: Pressures someone might laugh off or treat as trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make light of' looks like the idiom for treating lightly; read literally, these forces produce illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltage is electromotive force, the electrical push that drives a lamp's current.

clue.text: It's seen in perhaps every part of church

indicators.note: seen in says the letters can be spotted within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something found in nearly every section of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded recess, usually at the east end, of a church.

clue.text: School principal with aid to increase speed for bowler, say

parts.note: a head teacher is a school principal
changing gear on a bicycle or car helps you go faster

explanation.surface: A head teacher equipped with something to go faster, perhaps a cricket bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests cricket; it is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler hat is one example of something worn on the head.

clue.text: To take a course like this is humiliating

definitions.text: To take a course like this is humiliating

parts.words: To take a course like this is humiliating
parts.note: a course of a meal, here a dish of pie; eating this dish is the idiom for humbly admitting a mistake

explanation.surface: Following a certain path is a degrading experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a route or study programme, but it is a course of food.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a humble apology and accept humiliation.

clue.text: Fool wanting to be paid to admit parking

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so the owed word takes the next letter inside

parts.note: money due is owed, still to be paid
P is the standard abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A foolish person who wants payment for letting a car park.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe is to deceive or trick someone, the verb sense of fool.

clue.text: Former name to cause a stir

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: An old name now being used to stir things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite is to rouse or agitate, creating commotion.

clue.text: Tell king to cheer up

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
to elate is to make happy, cheer up

explanation.surface: Telling a monarch to brighten up.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate or recount it.

clue.text: Elegance of a foreign language

explanation.surface: The refinement found in some foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Refinement of style is polish; the Slavic tongue of Warsaw shares the spelling.

clue.text: A clay pit dug out of the common

indicators.note: dug suggests earth turned over, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A clay pit excavated out of common land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the common' reads as dug from common land, but it is the definition: out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means unusual, not ordinary, outside the norm.

clue.text: Put out of action, worriedly anticipate bill coming in

indicators.note: coming in says the bill piece enters the shuffled letters
worriedly suggests agitation, so the letters of anticipate are shaken up

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Nervously expecting a bill arriving that would disable you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worriedly' scrambles the fodder to INCAPITATE, and the account abbreviation goes into that after its fifth letter; 'bill' is an account, not a beak or a law.
explanation.definitionFit: To incapacitate is to disable or render unable to function.

clue.text: Give US intelligence a ring goodbye!

parts.note: the CIA is the American Central Intelligence Agency
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Phone the American spies and then sign off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a ring' suggests a phone call; the ring is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word is a casual farewell, also used for hello.

clue.text: Smokes when in prison

parts.note: British prison slang for tobacco, used as currency inside

explanation.surface: An inmate lighting up behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, especially in jails, the word for tobacco is the same as a pig's nose.

clue.text: Let it stand in toothpaste tube

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Leave something in its toothpaste tube.
explanation.definitionFit: The proofreader's Latin mark means let the deleted text remain.

clue.text: It shows the way to create a right rumpus

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel, a rumpus

explanation.surface: A signpost that sets off a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointing sign directs travellers in the correct direction.

clue.text: Wire that may hold back a ship

definitions.meaning: an insulated wire or bundle of wires carrying power or signals

definitions.text: that may hold back a ship
definitions.meaning: a ship's anchor rope or chain, which holds it in place

explanation.surface: A wire strong enough to restrain a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulated wiring and a ship's heavy anchor rope both carry this name.

clue.text: Stars get a breather when working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Celebrities get a rest between jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like celebrities; it is the constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Major is a northern constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Moves ship that's been raised and steered in an awkward position

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to warp a ship is to haul it along by ropes, so warps means moves a ship
led means guided or steered

explanation.surface: Shifts a lifted, guided boat into an ungainly spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's been raised' turns WARPS into SPRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprawled describes limbs spread out untidily, lying awkwardly.

clue.text: Achievement sure to be written about in newspaper articles

parts.note: a feat is an achievement

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters of sure are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: An accomplishment certain to get press coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Features are longer special articles in a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: For a time, it naturally puts us completely in the shade

definitions.text: For a time, it naturally puts us completely in the shade

parts.words: For a time, it naturally puts us completely in the shade
parts.note: when the moon fully blocks the sun, nature briefly plunges us into darkness

explanation.surface: Something that temporarily outshines us all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts in the shade' sounds like outdoing someone; literally, the moon's shadow covers us.
explanation.definitionFit: During a full solar event the moon hides the whole sun for minutes.

clue.text: Some powerful maritime bird

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A strong seagoing bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The fulmar is a grey and white seabird related to petrels.

clue.text: Two chaps, one customer

parts.note: Pat is a man's name
Ron is another man's name

explanation.surface: Two men, but only one of them buys.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular client of a shop or restaurant.

clue.text: Erect as this tree

parts.note: up means upright, erect

explanation.surface: Standing tall like this tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a poisonous Javanese tree of legend.

clue.text: Show appreciation of that figure

parts.note: to dig something is slang for enjoying it
it stands for that thing

explanation.surface: Express admiration for a certain shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a single numeral from nought to nine.

clue.text: Actors, and what they want to be

definitions.meaning: the company of performers in a play
performers hope to be chosen for a part, i.e. given a role

explanation.definitionFit: The performers in a production and the verb for assigning them roles share the word.

clue.text: Opinion survey?

definitions.meaning: a personal judgement or point of ...
to look over, inspect or survey a scene

explanation.definitionFit: A point of view and the act of looking over something share this word.

clue.text: An overhead light

parts.note: the ring of light shown above a saint's head, overhead in the literal sense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead light' suggests a ceiling lamp; it is the glow above a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint's glowing ring hovers just above the head in paintings.

clue.text: On the verge of alarming changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the next word are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: On the brink of frightening developments.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginal means at the edge or margin, so on the verge or border.

clue.text: Guest for the bingo official

definitions.meaning: a visitor who calls at a house
the person who reads out the numbers at bingo

explanation.surface: A visitor brought in to run the bingo game.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor at the door and the person announcing numbers at a bingo hall share the name.

clue.text: Famous place for divorcees with West End set

parts.note: Reno, Nevada, was famed for quick divorces

indicators.note: set means arranged, so the letters of end are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrated haunt of the newly divorced, linked to London's theatreland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district but splits in two, the second word reordered by 'set'. Reno, Nevada, was once the US capital of quick divorces.
explanation.definitionFit: Renowned means widely known and celebrated.

clue.text: When speaking, gathers crowds

indicators.note: when speaking says the word should be heard, not read

parts.note: hoards means stores up, gathers

explanation.surface: As one talks, people come together in throngs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hordes are large crowds or swarms of people.
